title.zh: 卷401 列傳一百八十八 向荣 和春 张国梁
title.en: Volume 401 Biographies 188: Xiang Rong, He Chun, Zhang Guoliang
title.raw: 卷401 列傳一百八十八 向荣 和春 张国梁

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十八向榮，字欣然，四川大寧人，寄籍甘肅固原。

translations.literal: Biography 188: Xiang Rong, style name Xinran, a native of Daning in Sichuan, with registered domicile at Guyuan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 188: Xiang Rong, courtesy name Xinran, was a native of Daning in Sichuan, with his registered domicile at Guyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 以行伍隸提標，為提督楊遇春所識拔。

translations.literal: He entered service as a common soldier under the provincial commander's banner and was recognized and promoted by Grand Coordinator Yang Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a rank-and-file soldier in the provincial commander's establishment, where Grand Coordinator Yang Yuchun noticed his ability and brought him forward.

sentences.zh: 從征滑縣、青海、回疆，常為選鋒。

translations.literal: He campaigned in Huaxian, Qinghai, and the Muslim borderlands, and was often chosen as assault vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in campaigns in Huaxian, Qinghai, and the Muslim frontier regions, and was repeatedly selected to lead the assault troops.

sentences.zh: 積功擢至甘肅鎮羌營游擊。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to colonel of the Zhenqiang battalion in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated merit he rose to the rank of colonel commanding the Zhenqiang battalion in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，直隸總督琦善知其才，調司教練，累遷開州協副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang, Zhili Governor-General Qishan recognized his talent, transferred him to oversee training, and he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Kaizhou Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Daoguang reign (1833), Governor-General Qishan of Zhili recognized his ability, put him in charge of drill and training, and he was promoted in stages until he became deputy commander of the Kaizhou Brigade.

sentences.zh: 海疆戒嚴，率兵駐防山海關。

translations.literal: When the maritime frontier was placed under martial alert, he led troops to garrison Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When the coast was put on military alert, he led troops to garrison Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 擢正定鎮總兵，調通永鎮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander of Zhengding garrison and transferred to Tongyong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the Zhengding garrison and transferred to command the Tongyong garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，擢四川提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the reign he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，調湖南，平李沅發之亂，調固原。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to Hunan, pacified Li Yuanfa's rebellion, and was then transferred to Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was posted to Hunan, where he put down the rebellion of Li Yuanfa, and was afterward transferred to Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 廣西匪起，巡撫鄭祖琛不能制。

translations.literal: Banditry broke out in Guangxi; Governor Zheng Zuochen could not suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Guangxi, Governor Zheng Zuochen proved unable to bring it under control.

sentences.zh: 榮於舊將中最負時望，文宗特調為廣西提督，倚以辦賊。

translations.literal: Among veteran generals Rong enjoyed the greatest contemporary reputation; Emperor Wenzong specially transferred him as Guangxi Grand Coordinator, relying on him to handle the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Among the senior commanders, Rong enjoyed the highest standing at court; Emperor Wenzong specially transferred him to serve as Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and placed the suppression of the rebels in his hands.

sentences.zh: 是秋至軍，由柳州、慶遠進剿，以達宜山、象州，連破賊於索潭墟、八旺、陶鄧墟、猶山等處，賊氛稍戢。

translations.literal: That autumn he reached the army; advancing from Liuzhou and Qingyuan in suppression, he reached Yishan and Xiangzhou, repeatedly defeating the bandits at Suotanxu, Bawang, Taodengxu, Youshan, and other places; the bandit menace was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he joined the army and advanced from Liuzhou and Qingyuan against the rebels, reaching Yishan and Xiangzhou. He won a series of victories at Suotanxu, Bawang, Taodengxu, Youshan, and other places, and the rebellion subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 惟洪秀全等踞桂平金田，狡悍為諸賊冠。

translations.literal: Only Hong Xiuquan and his band held Jintian in Guiping, the most crafty and fierce among all the bandit leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hong Xiuquan and his followers, entrenched at Jintian in Guiping, remained—the craftiest and most formidable of all the rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 榮移兵往剿，賊以大黃江、牛排嶺為犄角。

translations.literal: Rong shifted troops to suppress them; the bandits used Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong moved his forces against them, but the rebels used the Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge as mutually supporting strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，攻大黃江，賊分出誘戰，率總兵李能臣、周鳳岐合擊，大破之，殲千數百人，賜號霍欽巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xianfeng he attacked Dahuang River; the bandits sent out a detachment to lure combat, and he led Major Generals Li Nengchen and Zhou Fengqi in a combined strike, inflicting a great defeat and killing over a thousand; he was granted the designation Hojen Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Xianfeng he attacked the Dahuang River position. The rebels sent out a detachment to draw him into battle, but he led Major Generals Li Nengchen and Zhou Fengqi in a joint assault that routed them and killed more than a thousand. He was granted the honorific title Hojen Baturu.

sentences.zh: 水陸合攻牛排嶺，搗其巢，又追擊於新墟、紫金山，賊乃竄踞武宣東鄉。

translations.literal: Land and naval forces jointly attacked Niupai Ridge and stormed their nest; he pursued them further at Xin Market and Purple Gold Mountain, and the bandits then fled to occupy Dongxiang in Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He combined land and river forces to attack Niupai Ridge and destroy their base, then pursued them at Xin Market and Purple Gold Mountain until the rebels fled to Dongxiang in Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 時周天爵為巡撫，與榮同勦賊，議不合，數戰未得利，廣州副都統烏蘭泰率兵來會。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Tianjue was governor; he and Rong jointly suppressed the bandits, but their plans did not agree and several battles brought no success. Guangzhou Deputy Commander-in-Chief Ulangtai led troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Tianjue was then campaigning alongside Rong, but they could not agree on strategy and several engagements failed to gain ground. Deputy Commander-in-Chief Ulangtai of Guangzhou arrived with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊突圍竄象州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the bandits broke through the encirclement and fled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels broke out of the encirclement and fled toward Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮被譴，褫花翎，降三級留任，天爵亦罷軍事。

translations.literal: Rong was reprimanded, stripped of his peacock feather, demoted three ranks but retained in office; Tianjue was also removed from military command.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was censured, stripped of his peacock feather, and demoted three ranks while kept in post; Tianjue was likewise relieved of military duties.

sentences.zh: 大學士賽尚阿代李星沅督師，命榮與烏蘭泰節制鎮將以下，迭詔戒榮同心協力，以贖前愆。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Saishanga replaced Li Xingyuan in supreme command; Rong and Ulangtai were ordered to control all commanders of garrisons and below. Repeated edicts admonished Rong to work in concert and atone for his earlier faults.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Saishanga replaced Li Xingyuan as supreme commander and placed Rong and Ulangtai in charge of all field officers. The throne repeatedly urged Rong to cooperate wholeheartedly and redeem his earlier failures.

sentences.zh: 賊踞象州中坪，其要路東曰桐木，西曰羅秀，榮與烏蘭泰分扼之。

translations.literal: The bandits held Zhongping in Xiangzhou; the vital routes east were Tongmu and west Luoxiu; Rong and Ulangtai divided forces to block them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zhongping in Xiangzhou. The key routes east and west were Tongmu and Luoxiu respectively, and Rong and Ulangtai divided their forces to hold them.

sentences.zh: 六月，榮由桐木進兵，偕烏蘭泰合剿，迭敗賊於馬鞍山及架村、黃瓜嶺、西安村，遂回竄桂平新墟、紫金山，恃險負嵎。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Rong advanced from Tongmu; together with Ulangtai he jointly suppressed the bandits, repeatedly defeating them at Ma'an Mountain, Jiacun, Huanggualing, and Xi'an Village. The bandits then fled back to Xin Market and Purple Gold Mountain in Guiping, relying on rugged terrain to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Rong advanced from Tongmu and, together with Ulangtai, won a series of victories at Ma'an Mountain, Jiacun, Huanggualing, and Xi'an Village. The rebels then withdrew to Xin Market and Purple Gold Mountain in Guiping, where they dug in behind difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 榮偕烏蘭泰等迭奪豬仔峽、雙髻山要隘，進破風門坳。

translations.literal: Rong, together with Ulangtai and others, repeatedly seized the strategic passes at Zhuzai Gorge and Shuangji Mountain, and advanced to break Fengmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Ulangtai in turn captured the strategic passes at Zhuzai Gorge and Shuangji Mountain and pushed forward to break through Fengmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊冒雨竄逸，官軍失利於官村，遂陷永安州，坐褫職留營。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the bandits broke out in a rainstorm; government forces were defeated at Guancun, and Yong'an Prefecture fell. Rong was stripped of office but retained in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels broke out in heavy rain. Government forces were defeated at Guancun, and Yong'an Prefecture fell. Rong was stripped of his rank but allowed to remain with the army.

sentences.zh: 十一月，合攻永安，獲勝，復原官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they jointly attacked Yong'an, gained victory, and his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a joint assault on Yong'an succeeded, and his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 初，榮所部湖南兵，因榮子繼雄用事，軍心不服，故武宣、象州之役戰不力，皆歸咎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, among Rong's Hunan troops, because his son Jixiong wielded power, the army was discontented; therefore in the campaigns at Wuxuan and Xiangzhou they fought without vigor, and all blame was laid on this.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's Hunan troops had grown resentful because his son Jixiong was meddling in army affairs, and this was widely blamed for their poor performance in the battles at Wuxuan and Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宗排眾議，仍加倚任，而調四川兵以易湖南兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong set aside popular opinion and continued to rely on him, but transferred Sichuan troops to replace the Hunan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong overrode the critics and continued to place his trust in Rong, but replaced the Hunan troops with forces from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿不知兵，專倚榮與烏蘭泰。

translations.literal: Saishanga knew nothing of warfare and relied exclusively on Rong and Ulangtai.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga had no military experience and depended entirely on Rong and Ulangtai.

sentences.zh: 二人復不協，圍永安久不下。

translations.literal: The two men again failed to cooperate, and the siege of Yong'an long went unconquered.
translations.idiomatic: The two men again failed to work together, and the siege of Yong'an dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 榮建議缺北隅勿攻，伺賊逸擊之。

translations.literal: Rong proposed leaving the northern corner unassailed and waiting to strike when the bandits broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Rong proposed leaving the northern sector unblocked so that when the rebels tried to break out, they could be struck down in the open.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，天大雨，賊由北突出，迳犯桂林。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year there was heavy rain; the bandits broke out from the north and marched straight against Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, amid torrential rain, the rebels broke out to the north and marched directly on Guilin.

sentences.zh: 榮由間道馳援，先賊至，賊冒榮旗幟襲城，擊走之。

translations.literal: Rong rushed to relieve the city by a side road and arrived before the bandits. The bandits disguised themselves under Rong's banners to assault the city, but he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hurried to the city's relief by a side road and arrived ahead of the rebels. The rebels tried to enter under his banners, but he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫鄒鳴鶴急治守具，屢出奇兵擊賊城下，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Zou Minghe he urgently prepared defenses, repeatedly sent surprise forces to strike the bandits below the walls, and captured and slew a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Governor Zou Minghe he urgently strengthened the defenses and repeatedly sent raiding parties against the rebels below the walls, capturing and killing large numbers.

sentences.zh: 經月餘，援軍集，賊乃解圍北竄。

translations.literal: After more than a month relief armies gathered, and the bandits then lifted the siege and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, reinforcements arrived and the rebels raised the siege and fled north.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其保城功，已奪職復之，予議敘。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit in defending the city; his stripped office was restored and he was granted consideration for reward.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended him for saving the city, restored the rank that had been taken from him, and ordered that his merits be recorded for reward.

sentences.zh: 賊由興安、全州入湖南。

translations.literal: The bandits entered Hunan by way of Xing'an and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered Hunan through Xing'an and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮頓兵桂林，為總督徐廣縉論劾，褫職戍新疆。

translations.literal: Rong halted his army at Guilin; Governor-General Xu Guangjin memorialized against him, and he was stripped of office and banished to garrison duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had halted his army at Guilin. Governor-General Xu Guangjin impeached him, and he was stripped of rank and sentenced to exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿疏請暫緩發遣，令援湖南。

translations.literal: Saishanga memorialized asking that his dispatch be temporarily delayed and that he be ordered to relieve Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga petitioned that Rong's exile be postponed and that he be sent to reinforce Hunan instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，至長沙，破賊瀏陽門外，又破之於見家河、漁網洲、岳麓山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Changsha, defeated the bandits outside the Liuyang Gate, and defeated them again at Jianjia River, Yuwangzhou, and Yuelu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Changsha, defeated the rebels outside the Liuyang Gate, and won further victories at Jianjia River, Yuwangzhou, and Yuelu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至冬，圍乃解。

translations.literal: By winter the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the siege had been raised.

sentences.zh: 賊北竄，陷岳州，入湖北，進犯漢陽、武昌，官軍遙尾之，莫敢擊。

translations.literal: The bandits fled north, captured Yuezhou, entered Hubei, and advanced against Hanyang and Wuchang. Government forces followed at a distance and none dared attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled north, took Yuezhou, entered Hubei, and advanced on Hanyang and Wuchang. Government troops followed at a distance but dared not engage.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿、徐廣縉先後罷黜，諸將無一能軍。

translations.literal: Saishanga and Xu Guangjin were dismissed in succession; among the generals not one could command an army.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga and Xu Guangjin were dismissed one after another, and none of the remaining generals proved capable of holding the field.

sentences.zh: 詔以榮屢保危城，緩急尚欲恃之，予提督銜，幫辦軍務，責援武昌。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Rong had repeatedly defended endangered cities and was still to be relied on in crisis, he was granted the rank of Grand Coordinator, assigned to assist in military affairs, and charged to relieve Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne noted that Rong had repeatedly saved cities in peril and that he was still needed in an emergency. He was given the rank of Grand Coordinator, assigned to assist in military affairs, and ordered to relieve Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 尋复授廣西提督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 榮至，數奏捷，而武昌尋陷，褫職，仍留軍。

translations.literal: When Rong arrived he reported several victories, but Wuchang soon fell; he was stripped of office yet retained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong arrived he reported several victories, but Wuchang soon fell. He was stripped of rank but allowed to remain with the army.

sentences.zh: 調署湖北提督，未幾實授，命為欽差大臣，專辦軍務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to act as Grand Coordinator of Hubei; before long he received the substantive appointment and was made Imperial Commissioner with sole charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as acting Grand Coordinator of Hubei, soon received the substantive appointment, and was named Imperial Commissioner with sole responsibility for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 賊既踞武昌，勢益熾，不可復制矣。

translations.literal: Once the bandits held Wuchang their power grew ever fiercer and could no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels held Wuchang, their power grew overwhelming and could no longer be brought under control.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，大舉東犯，連舟蔽江，棄城而去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year they launched a great eastern offensive; boats lined the river in unbroken ranks, and they abandoned the city and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year they launched a major eastern offensive. Their fleet filled the river from bank to bank as they abandoned the city and marched east.

sentences.zh: 榮以克復聞，詔促躡追。

translations.literal: Rong reported the recovery; an edict urged him to pursue in close pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Rong reported that the city had been recovered, and the throne ordered him to pursue the rebels without delay.

sentences.zh: 榮所部兵多疲弱，遣撤六千餘名，料簡精銳，率總兵和春、李瑞、秦定三、玉山、福興沿江躡賊；

translations.literal: Many of Rong's troops were weak and worn; he sent away over six thousand, selected the elite, and led Major Generals He Chun, Li Rui, Qin Ding'er, Yushan, and Fuxing in pursuit along the river after the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Rong's troops were weak and demoralized. He dismissed more than six thousand, kept only the best, and led Major Generals He Chun, Li Rui, Qin Ding'er, Yushan, and Fuxing in pursuit along the river.

sentences.zh: 令提督蘇布通阿率川兵，總兵晉德布率滇兵來會。

translations.literal: He ordered Grand Coordinator Subutong'a to lead Sichuan troops and Major General Jindebu to lead Yunnan troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand Coordinator Subutong'a to bring Sichuan troops and Major General Jindebu to bring Yunnan forces to rendezvous with his army.

sentences.zh: 至九江，無舟，留半月，賊已掠安慶，陷江寧，為久踞計。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiujiang, he had no boats and remained half a month; the bandits had already raided Anqing, captured Jiangning, and planned a long occupation.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang he found no boats and was held up for half a month. Meanwhile the rebels had sacked Anqing, taken Jiangning, and were settling in for a long occupation.

sentences.zh: 榮至江寧，屯孝陵衛。

translations.literal: Rong reached Jiangning and encamped at Xiaoling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rong reached Jiangning and encamped at the Xiaoling Guard post.

sentences.zh: 時鎮江、揚州皆為賊踞，詔琦善剿江北，榮剿江南，分任軍事。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenjiang and Yangzhou were both held by bandits; an edict ordered Qishan to suppress the north of the river and Rong the south, dividing military responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang and Yangzhou were both in rebel hands. Qishan was ordered to campaign north of the river and Rong south of it, dividing command of the war.

sentences.zh: 榮所部一萬七千餘人，攻通濟門外及七橋甕賊壘，連破之，進屯紫金山，結營十八座，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Rong's force of more than seventeen thousand attacked the bandit stockades outside Tongji Gate and at Qiqiao'ao, repeatedly breaking them, advanced to encamp on Purple Gold Mountain, established eighteen camps, and was granted a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's force of more than seventeen thousand men attacked the rebel stockades outside Tongji Gate and at Qiqiao'ao, broke them in succession, and advanced to encamp on Purple Gold Mountain, where he established eighteen camps. He was awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 江寧城內士民謀結合內應，屢爽期，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Inside Jiangning gentry and commoners plotted coordinated uprisings, but dates were repeatedly missed and nothing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Jiangning, local gentry and townspeople plotted coordinated uprisings, but the plans repeatedly fell through and never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 賊已分股由安徽北擾河南，而鎮江、揚州南北互應，大江上下游賊勢相首尾。

translations.literal: The bandits had already split forces from Anhui to raid north into Henan, while Zhenjiang and Yangzhou responded to each other north and south; up and down the Great River the bandit power linked head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel detachments had already moved north from Anhui into Henan, while Zhenjiang and Yangzhou coordinated with each other across the river. Rebel strength up and down the Yangtze formed a continuous chain.

sentences.zh: 榮遣提督鄧紹良率兵八千規鎮江，總兵和春以舟師伺便夾擊，屢戰，進壁城下。

translations.literal: Rong sent Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang with eight thousand troops to threaten Zhenjiang; Major General He Chun with the fleet waited for opportunity to strike from both sides. After repeated battles they advanced and walled up below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang with eight thousand men to threaten Zhenjiang, while Major General He Chun's fleet waited for a chance to strike from the river. After several engagements they advanced and built siege lines below the walls.

sentences.zh: 六月，紹良軍為賊所襲，退守丹徒鎮，榮令和春往援，遂代領其軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Shaoliang's army was attacked by bandits and withdrew to defend Dantu Town. Rong ordered He Chun to relieve them and then took command of that army himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Deng Shaoliang's force was ambushed and fell back to Dantu. Rong sent He Chun to reinforce him and then took personal command of the army.

sentences.zh: 賊注意蘇、常諸郡，以和春軍相持不得進，乃欲取道東壩。

translations.literal: The bandits set their sights on the prefectures of Suzhou and Changzhou; blocked by He Chun's army they could not advance, and therefore wished to take the route through Dongba.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned their attention to Suzhou and Changzhou. Blocked by He Chun's army, they sought to advance by way of Dongba instead.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊船入蕪湖，陷高淳，遣兵擊走之，令鄧紹良駐防。

translations.literal: In the tenth month bandit boats entered Wuhu and captured Gaochun; he sent troops to drive them off and ordered Deng Shaoliang to garrison the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month rebel boats entered Wuhu and took Gaochun. He sent troops to drive them off and stationed Deng Shaoliang to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 既而皖北賊熾，和春赴援，榮請以提督餘萬清代督鎮江軍。

translations.literal: Before long banditry flared in northern Anhui; He Chun went to relieve it, and Rong requested that Grand Coordinator Yu Wanqing act in command of the Zhenjiang army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel activity then intensified in northern Anhui, and He Chun went to reinforce that front. Rong asked that Grand Coordinator Yu Wanqing take over command of the Zhenjiang army.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，賊犯東壩，遣副將傅振邦等協剿，賊退高淳，進復其城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year bandits attacked Dongba; he sent Brigadier General Fu Zhenbang and others in joint suppression; the bandits withdrew to Gaochun, and he advanced to recover the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year the rebels attacked Dongba. He sent Brigadier General Fu Zhenbang and others against them. The rebels fell back to Gaochun, and government forces advanced and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 賊乘江寧大營空虛，大舉來撲，率諸軍拒之，擒偽丞相譚應桂，俘斬三千餘。

translations.literal: The bandits took advantage of the Jiangning main camp being empty and came in force to assault it; he led the armies to resist, captured the false chancellor Tan Yinggui, and took or slew more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels exploited the weakness of the Jiangning headquarters and launched a major assault. Rong led the armies in defense, captured the rebel chancellor Tan Yinggui, and killed or captured more than three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 總兵葉長春、吳全美以水師克下關水柵砲台，殪偽燕王秦日綱，進扼三山，營江路上游。

translations.literal: Major Generals Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei with the fleet captured the water barrier and batteries at Xiaguan, killed the false Prince of Yan Qin Rigang, advanced to hold Sanshan, and encamped on the upper reaches of the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Major Generals Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei with the naval force captured the water barrier and batteries at Xiaguan, killed the rebel Prince of Yan Qin Rigang, advanced to hold Sanshan, and established camps on the upper river.

sentences.zh: 賊聚太平府，與江寧相應。

translations.literal: The bandits gathered at Taiping Prefecture in mutual support with Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels concentrated at Taiping Prefecture in coordination with the forces at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 張國樑連克賊壘，乘勝复太平，殲賊首韋得真等。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang repeatedly captured bandit stockades, pressed the victory to recover Taiping, and annihilated bandit leaders including Wei Dezheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang captured one rebel stockade after another, followed up his victories to recover Taiping, and killed rebel leaders including Wei Dezheng.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊出營於上方橋，三路來撲，又撲七橋甕，分擊敗之，三戰殪賊二萬餘。

translations.literal: Jiangning bandits came out of camp at Shangfang Bridge and assaulted in three columns; they assaulted again at Qiqiao'ao; divided forces struck and defeated them; in three battles over twenty thousand bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces from Jiangning sallied from Shangfang Bridge in three columns and again attacked at Qiqiao'ao. Government forces met them in divided assaults and, in three engagements, killed more than twenty thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 八月，毀上方橋賊壘，進逼雨花台，搗其巢，追奔至城下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he destroyed the bandit stockades at Shangfang Bridge, advanced to press Yuhuatai, stormed their nest, and pursued the rout to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he destroyed the rebel stockades at Shangfang Bridge, advanced on Yuhuatai, stormed their base, and pursued the fleeing rebels to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 賊復由觀音門出趨棲霞，令總兵德安追擊，敗之於高資汛，又與餘萬清合擊於夾江，擒斬殆盡。

translations.literal: The bandits again came out through Guanyin Gate toward Qixia; he ordered Major General De'an to pursue, defeated them at Gaozi Ford, and jointly with Yu Wanqing struck at Jiajiang, capturing and slaying nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied again through Guanyin Gate toward Qixia. Rong ordered Major General De'an to pursue, routed them at Gaozi Ford, and together with Yu Wanqing struck them at Jiajiang, capturing or killing nearly all.

sentences.zh: 萬清亦屢敗賊於鎮江。

translations.literal: Wanqing also repeatedly defeated bandits at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanqing also won repeated victories over the rebels at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 五年春，湖北竄賊入蕪湖，鄧紹良御之於黃池。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year marauding bandits from Hubei entered Wuhu; Deng Shaoliang met them at Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, rebel raiders from Hubei entered Wuhu, and Deng Shaoliang met them at Huangchi.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲賊出鮎魚套犯高資，擊走之。

translations.literal: Bandits from Guazhou came out of Nianyu Bend to attack Gaozi; he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Guazhou came out of Nianyu Bend to attack Gaozi, but were driven back.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊由蕪湖犯灣沚，卻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month bandits from Wuhu attacked Wanzhi; he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebels from Wuhu attacked Wanzhi, but were repulsed.

sentences.zh: 吳全美率水師破賊於東梁山，德安、明安泰率陸師進攻蕪湖，會鄧紹良大破安慶援賊，遂復蕪湖。

translations.literal: Wu Quanmei led the fleet to defeat bandits at Dongliang Mountain; De'an and Ming'antai led the land force to attack Wuhu; joining Deng Shaoliang in a great defeat of Anqing relief bandits, they then recovered Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quanmei with the fleet defeated the rebels at Dongliang Mountain, while De'an and Ming'antai led the land force against Wuhu. Together with Deng Shaoliang, who routed the Anqing relief force, they recovered Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 餘賊猶濱江結壘，以廣福磯、弋磯為犄角，數路死力來援，紹良、全美等水陸苦戰，迭敗之而不能克也。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits still built stockades along the river, using Guangfu Rock and Yi Rock as pincers; relief came by several routes with desperate force; Shaoliang, Quanmei, and others fought bitterly by land and water, repeatedly defeating them yet unable to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining rebels still held riverbank stockades, using Guangfu Rock and Yi Rock as mutually supporting positions. Reinforcements arrived by several routes and fought desperately. Deng Shaoliang, Wu Quanmei, and others battled hard by land and water, winning repeated victories but failing to take the positions.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫吉爾杭阿既克上海，詔幫辦軍務，專任鎮江一路，督攻甚急，江寧賊百計赴援。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Ji'erhang'a had already recovered Shanghai; an edict assigned him to assist in military affairs with sole charge of the Zhenjiang route, pressing the attack urgently; Jiangning bandits used every stratagem to send relief.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ji'erhang'a had just recovered Shanghai and was ordered to assist in military affairs with sole responsibility for the Zhenjiang front. He pressed the attack hard, and the rebels at Jiangning used every means to send reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 十一月，榮督總兵德安、張國樑、秦如虎等，迭擊之於燕子磯、觀音門、甘家港、棲霞街、石埠橋等處，賊竄回江寧，令德安駐軍東陽鎮扼之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Rong directed Major Generals De'an, Zhang Guoliang, Qin Ruhu, and others in repeated strikes at Yanziji, Guanyin Gate, Ganjiagang, Qixia Street, and Shibuqiao; the bandits fled back to Jiangning, and he ordered De'an to garrison Dongyang Town to block them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Rong directed Major Generals De'an, Zhang Guoliang, and Qin Ruhu in a series of attacks at Yanziji, Guanyin Gate, Ganjiagang, Qixia Street, and Shibuqiao. The rebels fled back toward Jiangning, and he stationed De'an at Dongyang Town to block their retreat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上游蕪湖、兩梁山、金柱關及江北瓜洲、金山、廬州、三河諸賊同趨江寧，約城中悍賊衝出：一由神策門至仙鶴門抄綴大營；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month bandits from upriver at Wuhu, Liangliang Mountain, Jinzhuguan, and north of the river at Guazhou, Jinshan, Luzhou, Sanhe, and elsewhere all converged on Jiangning, coordinating with fierce bandits in the city to break out: one column from Shece Gate to Xianhe Gate to strike at the rear of the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month rebels from upriver at Wuhu, Liangliang Mountain, and Jinzhuguan, together with forces from north of the river at Guazhou, Jinshan, Luzhou, Sanhe, and elsewhere, all converged on Jiangning in concert with a breakout from the city. One column was to move from Shece Gate to Xianhe Gate and strike the rear of the main camp.

sentences.zh: 一由觀音門沿江至棲霞，直趨鎮江；

translations.literal: One column from Guanyin Gate along the river to Qixia, marching straight on Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: A second column was to move from Guanyin Gate along the river to Qixia and strike directly at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 一由南路秣陵關來犯。

translations.literal: One column from the southern route through Muling Pass to attack.
translations.idiomatic: A third was to attack from the south through Muling Pass.

sentences.zh: 榮令張國樑、秦如虎迎擊於仙鶴門，大捷，回擊石埠橋，賊亦退，又敗之於龍脖子及元山、板橋等處。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu to meet them at Xianhe Gate with a great victory; turning back he struck at Shibuqiao and the bandits also withdrew; he defeated them again at Longbozi, Yuanshan, Banqiao, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Rong ordered Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu to meet them at Xianhe Gate and won a major victory. They then turned back to strike at Shibuqiao, where the rebels also retreated, and won further victories at Longbozi, Yuanshan, Banqiao, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 檄鄧紹良自蕪湖回援，餘萬清自鎮江移駐龍潭、下蜀街。

translations.literal: He summoned Deng Shaoliang from Wuhu to return in relief; Yu Wanqing moved from Zhenjiang to garrison Longtan and Xiashu Street.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Deng Shaoliang from Wuhu and shifted Yu Wanqing from Zhenjiang to garrison Longtan and Xiashu Street.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊踞倉頭，為往來要道，餘萬清、張國樑迭擊不退，鄧紹良至，令統前敵諸軍，屢戰不利。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year bandits held Cangtou, a vital route of passage; Yu Wanqing and Zhang Guoliang repeatedly attacked without driving them off. When Deng Shaoliang arrived, he was ordered to command all front-line armies, but several battles went badly.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels held Cangtou, a key junction on the main route. Yu Wanqing and Zhang Guoliang attacked repeatedly without dislodging them. When Deng Shaoliang arrived he was placed in command of the front-line forces, but several engagements went against the government troops.

sentences.zh: 賊日增多，蔓延炭渚、橋頭，改以張國樑為總統，國樑力戰，連破橋頭、下​​蜀街、三汊河、張楊村諸壘，賊始竄走，復合鎮江賊入瓜洲，將軍托明阿軍潰，江北大震。

translations.literal: Bandits increased daily, spreading to Tanzhu and Qiaotou; Zhang Guoliang was made overall commander. Guoliang fought fiercely, repeatedly breaking stockades at Qiaotou, Xiashu Street, San Cha River, and Zhangyang Village; the bandits then fled. They reunited with Zhenjiang bandits and entered Guazhou; General Tuo Ming'a's army collapsed and the north of the river was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew stronger by the day and spread to Tanzhu and Qiaotou. Zhang Guoliang was made overall commander and fought hard, capturing stockades at Qiaotou, Xiashu Street, San Cha River, and Zhangyang Village until the rebels finally fled. They then joined forces with the Zhenjiang rebels and entered Guazhou. General Tuo Ming'a's army collapsed, throwing the north bank into panic.

sentences.zh: 榮令紹良援揚州，偕德興阿復其城。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Shaoliang to relieve Yangzhou; together with Dexing'a he recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent Deng Shaoliang to relieve Yangzhou, and together with Dexing'a he recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 國梁援六合，進克江浦、浦口，江北稍定。

translations.literal: Guoliang relieved Liuhe, advanced to capture Jiangpu and Pukou, and the north of the river was somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang relieved Liuhe and advanced to take Jiangpu and Pukou, bringing a measure of calm back to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 四月，寧國告陷，蘇、浙戒嚴，令紹良馳御之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ningguo reported fallen; Suzhou and Zhejiang were placed on alert, and Shaoliang was ordered to rush to its defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month word came that Ningguo had fallen. Suzhou and Zhejiang were put on alert, and Deng Shaoliang was ordered to hurry to its defense.

sentences.zh: 江長貴亦退守黃池，而鎮江軍事复急。

translations.literal: Jiang Changgui also withdrew to defend Huangchi, while military affairs at Zhenjiang again grew urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Changgui also fell back to defend Huangchi, while the situation at Zhenjiang again grew critical.

sentences.zh: 國樑進攻小丹陽未下，吉爾杭阿戰歿於煙墩山，鎮江京峴山營壘皆失，榮令餘萬清代領其軍。

translations.literal: Guoliang attacked Xiaodanyang without taking it; Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle at Yandun Mountain; Zhenjiang camps at Jingxian Mountain were all lost; Rong ordered Yu Wanqing to take command of that army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang besieged Xiaodanyang without success. Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle at Yandun Mountain, and the government camps at Jingxian Mountain near Zhenjiang were lost. Rong placed Yu Wanqing in command of the army.

sentences.zh: 明安泰扼小丹陽，福興、張國樑率兵防剿，以固蘇、常門戶。

translations.literal: Ming'antai held Xiaodanyang; Fuxing and Zhang Guoliang led troops in defense and suppression to secure the gateways of Suzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'antai held Xiaodanyang while Fuxing and Zhang Guoliang led troops in defense and pursuit to secure the approaches to Suzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 國樑破賊於丹徒鎮，進扼馬陵，而賊已陷溧水，由高資、下蜀街趨江寧，分屯太平、神策門外。

translations.literal: Guoliang defeated bandits at Dantu Town and advanced to hold Maling, but bandits had already taken Lishui, moved from Gaozi and Xiashu Street toward Jiangning, and divided encampments outside Taiping and Shece Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang defeated the rebels at Dantu and advanced to hold Maling, but the rebels had already taken Lishui and were moving from Gaozi and Xiashu Street toward Jiangning, establishing positions outside Taiping and Shece Gate.

sentences.zh: 五月，上游賊麕至，屯城北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month upriver bandits gathered in crowds and encamped north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebel forces from upriver converged in great numbers and encamped north of the city.

sentences.zh: 榮大營兵僅數千，急促國樑回援。

translations.literal: Rong's main camp had only a few thousand troops; he urgently summoned Guoliang to return in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's headquarters had only a few thousand men left. He urgently recalled Zhang Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 賊分十餘路來撲，營壘盡失，退守淳化鎮，再退丹陽，自請治罪，詔原之，褫職，仍留欽差大臣，督辦軍務。

translations.literal: Bandits assaulted in more than ten columns; all camps were lost; he withdrew to defend Chunhua Town, then withdrew again to Danyang; he requested punishment; an edict pardoned him, stripped his office, yet retained him as Imperial Commissioner supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked in more than ten columns. All the camps were lost. Rong fell back to Chunhua, then to Danyang, and asked to be punished. The throne pardoned him but stripped his rank, while keeping him on as Imperial Commissioner in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 丹陽當鎮江、江寧兩路要衝，榮率張國樑、虎嵩林扼守。

translations.literal: Danyang stood at the vital junction of the Zhenjiang and Jiangning routes; Rong led Zhang Guoliang and Hu Songlin to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang lay at the strategic junction between the Zhenjiang and Jiangning fronts. Rong led Zhang Guoliang and Hu Songlin to hold the position.

sentences.zh: 令西林防句容，明安泰攻溧水，江長貴扼溧陽，張國樑仍總統諸軍。

translations.literal: He ordered Xilin to defend Jurong, Ming'antai to attack Lishui, Jiang Changgui to hold Liyang, and Zhang Guoliang remained overall commander of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xilin to defend Jurong, Ming'antai to attack Lishui, and Jiang Changgui to hold Liyang, while Zhang Guoliang remained overall commander.

sentences.zh: 賊更番至，恃國樑力禦卻之。

translations.literal: Bandits came in rotating waves; relying on Guoliang's strength they were held off and repelled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked in waves, but Zhang Guoliang's fierce resistance held them back.

sentences.zh: 疏請增兵，未至，榮憂憤成病，七月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting reinforcements, but they had not arrived; Rong fell ill from grief and anger; in the seventh month he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for reinforcements, but they had not arrived. Rong fell ill from grief and exhaustion, and in the seventh month he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，文宗震悼，詔嘉其忠勤，雖未恢復堅城，數年保障蘇、常，盡心竭力，復原官，依例賜卹，予一等輕車都尉世職，諡忠武。

translations.literal: His final memorial was submitted; Emperor Wenzong was deeply shaken; an edict praised his loyalty and diligence: although he had not recovered the fortified city, for several years he had secured Suzhou and Changzhou, exhausting heart and strength; his original office was restored, condolence grants were given according to regulation, he was granted a hereditary rank as First-class Commandant of Light Chariots, and given the posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong was deeply grieved. An edict praised his loyalty and devotion: though he had not recovered the walled city, for years he had shielded Suzhou and Changzhou and had given everything he had. His former rank was restored, standard mourning honors were granted, he was given the hereditary rank of First-class Commandant of Light Chariots, and the posthumous name Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).

sentences.zh: 命建專祠，又入祀江蘇名宦祠。

translations.literal: He was ordered a special shrine built, and also entered for worship in the Jiangsu shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a special shrine built in his honor and had him entered in the Jiangsu shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 克復江寧後，賜祭一壇，入昭忠祠。

translations.literal: After Jiangning was recovered, one altar of sacrifice was granted, and he was entered in the Zhao Zhong Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning was recovered, the court granted a sacrificial altar in his honor and enshrined him in the Zhao Zhong Shrine.

sentences.zh: 子繼雄，候選道，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Jixiong was an expectant circuit intendant and inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixiong, an expectant circuit intendant, inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 和春，字雨亭，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: He Chun, style name Yuting, of the Heseri clan, a bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun, courtesy name Yuting, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由前鋒、藍翎長授整儀尉，累遷副護軍參領。

translations.literal: From vanguard and blue-lance chief he was appointed ceremonial guard, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy banner guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a vanguard and blue-lance chief, he was appointed a ceremonial guard and rose in stages to deputy banner guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南提標中軍參將，擢永綏協副將。

translations.literal: He went out as second colonel of the Hunan commander's central army and was promoted deputy commander of the Yongshui Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as second colonel of the Hunan commander's central army and promoted to deputy commander of the Yongshui Brigade.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，從向榮赴廣西剿匪，戰武宣東鄉，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi to suppress bandits, fought at Dongxiang in Wuxuan, and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi to suppress the rebels, fought at Dongxiang in Wuxuan, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 破賊於中坪，進攻紫金山，奪雙髻山、豬仔峽要隘，功最，賜號鏗色巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He defeated bandits at Zhongping, advanced to attack Purple Gold Mountain, seized the strategic passes at Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge; his merit was greatest, and he was granted the designation Kengse Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels at Zhongping, advanced on Purple Gold Mountain, and captured the strategic passes at Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge. His achievements were the greatest of all, and he was granted the title Kengse Baturu.

sentences.zh: 又奪風門坳，克古調村賊巢，擢綏靖鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He also seized Fengmen Pass, captured the bandit nest at Gutiao Village, and was promoted commander of Suijing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Fengmen Pass and destroyed the rebel base at Gutiao Village, and was promoted to commander of the Suijing garrison.

sentences.zh: 二年，援桂林，力戰解圍，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the second year he relieved Guilin, fought fiercely to lift the siege, and was given the rank of Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he relieved Guilin, fought hard to raise the siege, and was given the rank of Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 追賊至全州，敗之。

translations.literal: He pursued bandits to Quanzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels to Quanzhou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊入湖南，迭戰於道州、桂陽，遂犯長沙，和春從向榮赴援，數出奇破賊。

translations.literal: Bandits entered Hunan and fought repeatedly at Daozhou and Guiyang, then attacked Changsha. He Chun followed Xiang Rong to relieve the city and repeatedly sent surprise forces to break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered Hunan and fought at Daozhou and Guiyang before advancing on Changsha. He Chun followed Xiang Rong to the relief of the city and repeatedly sent raiding parties that routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊去陷岳州，坐追剿遷延，褫職留軍。

translations.literal: The bandits departed and captured Yuezhou; for delay in pursuit he was stripped of office but retained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew and took Yuezhou. He Chun was stripped of rank for the delay in pursuit but allowed to remain with the army.

sentences.zh: 三年春，會攻武昌。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year they jointly attacked Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year they joined in the assault on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城東下，追至九江，遇賊，襲擊之。

translations.literal: The bandits abandoned the city and went east; he pursued to Jiujiang, encountered bandits, and attacked them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned the city and marched east. He pursued them to Jiujiang, encountered rebel forces, and attacked by surprise.

sentences.zh: 從向榮抵江寧，分軍攻通濟門外賊壘。

translations.literal: Following Xiang Rong he reached Jiangning and divided forces to attack bandit stockades outside Tongji Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xiang Rong he reached Jiangning and divided his forces to attack the rebel stockades outside Tongji Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋偕總兵葉長春、吳全美等率舟師攻鎮江，破賊甘露寺下。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, together with Major Generals Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei and others, he led the fleet to attack Zhenjiang and defeated bandits below Ganlu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, together with Major Generals Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei, he led the fleet against Zhenjiang and defeated the rebels below Ganlu Temple.

sentences.zh: 駐金山扼江路，又掠鮎魚套，擊敗賊船。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Jinshan to hold the river route, also raided Nianyu Bend, and defeated bandit boats.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Jinshan to control the river route, raided Nianyu Bend, and defeated rebel vessels.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵瞿騰龍攻太平門，填壕逼城，殲賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Together with Major General Qu Tenglong he attacked Taiping Gate, filled the moat to press the walls, and annihilated a great many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Major General Qu Tenglong he attacked Taiping Gate, filled in the moat to press the walls, and killed large numbers of rebels.

sentences.zh: 六月，提督鄧紹良師潰於鎮江，詔和春署江南提督，率所部廣東、湖南兵馳援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang's army collapsed at Zhenjiang; an edict appointed He Chun acting Grand Coordinator of Jiangnan and ordered him to lead his Guangdong and Hunan troops in haste to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Deng Shaoliang's army was routed at Zhenjiang. He Chun was appointed acting Grand Coordinator of Jiangnan and ordered to hurry to the relief with his Guangdong and Hunan troops.

sentences.zh: 移軍丹徒鎮，進复京峴山舊壘。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to Dantu Town and advanced to recover the old camps at Jingxian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his army to Dantu and advanced to recover the old camps at Jingxian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊數千來爭，殲戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Several thousand bandits came to contest the position; nearly all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand rebels came to contest the position, and nearly all were killed.

sentences.zh: 賊銳稍挫，兩軍相持，蘇、常得無事。

translations.literal: The bandits' edge was somewhat blunted; the two armies faced each other, and Suzhou and Changzhou remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' momentum was checked. The two armies settled into a stalemate, and Suzhou and Changzhou were spared further harm.

sentences.zh: 尋實授提督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he received the substantive appointment as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the substantive appointment as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，安徽軍事急，命和春分兵移防滁州，遂進援廬州。

translations.literal: That winter military affairs in Anhui grew urgent; He Chun was ordered to divide forces and shift defense to Chuzhou, then advance to relieve Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the military situation in Anhui grew critical. He Chun was ordered to detach troops to defend Chuzhou and then advance to relieve Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫江忠源困守危城，陝甘總督舒興阿率援軍至，不敢戰，忠源疏言和春忠勇可恃，請命總督援軍，詔允之，而所部僅千人，請舒興阿分兵，不聽。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Zhongyuan was besieged in a perilous city. Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Shuxing'a led relief troops but dared not fight. Zhongyuan memorialized that He Chun's loyalty and courage could be relied on and requested command of the governor-general's relief army; an edict approved, but his own force had only a thousand men; he asked Shuxing'a to divide troops, and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Zhongyuan was trapped in a desperate siege. Governor-General Shuxing'a of Shaanxi-Gansu arrived with reinforcements but would not fight. Zhongyuan memorialized that He Chun's loyalty and courage could be trusted and asked that the relief army be placed under his command. The throne agreed, but He Chun had only a thousand men and his request for troops from Shuxing'a was refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廬州陷，忠源殉。

translations.literal: Before long Luzhou fell and Zhongyuan died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luzhou fell, and Zhongyuan died defending it.

sentences.zh: 軍事專屬和春，福濟繼任巡撫，為之副。

translations.literal: Military affairs were placed solely under He Chun; Fu Ji succeeded as governor and served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Military command passed entirely to He Chun, while Fu Ji succeeded as governor and served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「皖省軍情重大，兵勇雖有萬餘，多未經戰陣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: 'Military conditions in Anhui are grave. Although troops number more than ten thousand, most have not seen battle.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he memorialized: 'The military situation in Anhui is grave. Although we have more than ten thousand troops, most have never seen combat.'

sentences.zh: 請調鎮江舊部湖南兵，並撥金陵得力官兵三千，交總兵秦定三、鄭魁士率之來助剿。

translations.literal: He requested transfer of his old Hunan troops from Zhenjiang and allocation of three thousand effective officers and soldiers from Jinling, to be led by Major Generals Qin Ding'er and Zheng Kuishi to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that his old Hunan troops from Zhenjiang be transferred, and that three thousand seasoned troops from Jinling be assigned to Major Generals Qin Ding'er and Zheng Kuishi to reinforce the campaign.

sentences.zh: 」時廬州屬縣皆陷，與安慶踞賊連絡一氣，城大賊眾，和春駐軍三里岡，屢率鄭魁士等進剿，賊抗拒不下。

translations.literal: 'At the time all subordinate counties of Luzhou had fallen; they linked with bandits holding Anqing as one force. The city was large and bandits numerous. He Chun encamped at Sanligang, repeatedly led Zheng Kuishi and others in advance suppression, but the bandits resisted and would not fall.'
translations.idiomatic: By then every county around Luzhou had fallen, and the rebels there were in close contact with those holding Anqing. The city was large and the rebel force numerous. He Chun encamped at Sanligang and repeatedly led Zheng Kuishi and others in attacks, but the rebels held firm.

sentences.zh: 乃沿河築壘構橋，分三路更番攻擊。

translations.literal: He then built stockades and bridges along the river and attacked in rotation by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: He then built stockades and bridges along the river and launched attacks in rotation along three routes.

sentences.zh: 夏，知州茅念劬率民團克六安，秦定三破賊於三連橋，進攻舒城。

translations.literal: In summer Prefect Mao Nianqu led militia to recover Lu'an; Qin Ding'er defeated bandits at Sanlian Bridge and advanced to attack Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Prefect Mao Nianqu led local militia to recover Lu'an, while Qin Ding'er defeated the rebels at Sanlian Bridge and advanced on Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 賊由霍山撲六安，擊走之。

translations.literal: Bandits from Huoshan rushed at Lu'an; he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Huoshan attacked Lu'an, but were driven back.

sentences.zh: 扎筏載大砲轟廬州城，賊分出拒戰，迭敗之。

translations.literal: He lashed rafts to carry great cannon to bombard Luzhou city; bandits sent out forces to resist, and he repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He built rafts to mount heavy cannon and bombard Luzhou. The rebels sent out forces to resist, and he defeated them in successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 別遣軍复英山、廬江，而和州、含山一路賊時窺伺，疏請飭袁甲三嚴防烏江，以斷賊援。

translations.literal: He separately sent armies to recover Yingshan and Lujiang, while bandits along the Hezhou and Hanshan route constantly watched for opportunity; he memorialized requesting that Yuan Jiasan strictly guard Wujiang to cut bandit relief.
translations.idiomatic: He sent other forces to recover Yingshan and Lujiang, while rebels along the Hezhou and Hanshan route kept probing for openings. He petitioned that Yuan Jiasan be ordered to hold Wujiang strictly and cut off rebel reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 冬，臧紆青、劉玉豹由廬南規桐城，連奪大關等隘，逼城下，而紆青戰歿，玉豹退保六安，和春為賊牽制不能救。

translations.literal: In winter Zang Yuqing and Liu Yubao from south of Lu threatened Tongcheng, repeatedly seized passes such as Daguan, and pressed below the walls; but Yuqing was killed in battle, Yubao withdrew to defend Lu'an, and He Chun was pinned by bandits and could not relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zang Yuqing and Liu Yubao advanced from south of Lu toward Tongcheng, capturing passes including Daguan and pressing the walls. Yuqing was killed in battle, Yubao fell back to defend Lu'an, and He Chun was too tied down to help.

sentences.zh: 秦定三攻舒城，亦久不下，迭詔切責。

translations.literal: Qin Ding'er's attack on Shucheng also long went unconquered, and repeated edicts sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ding'er's siege of Shucheng also dragged on without success, and the throne issued repeated stern rebukes.

sentences.zh: 初，和春專剿廬州，袁甲三扼臨淮，軍事多相關，而意不合。

translations.literal: Earlier He Chun had sole charge of suppressing Luzhou while Yuan Jiasan held Linhuai; military affairs were often interrelated, yet their views did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier He Chun had been solely responsible for the Luzhou campaign while Yuan Jiasan held Linhuai. Their operations were closely linked, but the two men could not agree.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕福濟疏劾甲三，罷之，命和春遣員接統其軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Fu Ji, he memorialized to impeach Jiasan; Jiasan was dismissed, and He Chun was ordered to send an officer to take over his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he and Fu Ji jointly impeached Yuan Jiasan, who was dismissed. He Chun was ordered to send an officer to take command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 夏秋連擊敗援賊，督諸軍急攻廬州，至十月克之，城陷將兩年矣。

translations.literal: Through summer and autumn he repeatedly defeated relief bandits, directed the armies in urgent attack on Luzhou, and by the tenth month captured it; the city had been fallen nearly two years.
translations.idiomatic: Through summer and autumn he repeatedly defeated rebel relief forces and pressed the assault on Luzhou. The city fell in the tenth month after nearly two years in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉和春功能補過，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised He Chun's merit as compensating for faults, granted a yellow jacket, and gave a hereditary rank as Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised He Chun for redeeming his earlier failures, awarded him the yellow jacket, and granted him the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 六年，复舒城，大破賊於三河，克之，再复廬江。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he recovered Shucheng, inflicted a great defeat on bandits at Sanhe and captured it, and again recovered Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he recovered Shucheng, won a major victory at Sanhe and took the town, and recovered Lujiang as well.

sentences.zh: 會向榮卒於軍，命和春代為欽差大臣，督辦江南軍務。

translations.literal: When Xiang Rong died in camp, He Chun was ordered to replace him as Imperial Commissioner supervising Jiangnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Rong died in camp, He Chun was appointed Imperial Commissioner in his place to direct military affairs in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 自向榮兵挫，退守丹陽，江寧賊益驕，內閧，自相殘殺，故榮歿後，張國樑等得以撫輯餘軍，規復東壩、高淳。

translations.literal: Since Xiang Rong's army had been defeated and withdrew to defend Danyang, Jiangning bandits grew more arrogant, quarreled internally, and slaughtered one another; therefore after Rong's death Zhang Guoliang and others were able to rally the remaining army and plan recovery of Dongba and Gaochun.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang Rong's defeat and withdrawal to Danyang, the rebels at Jiangning grew overconfident, fell to infighting, and slaughtered one another. This allowed Zhang Guoliang and others, after Rong's death, to rally the remaining forces and plan the recovery of Dongba and Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 和春至，餉械並絀，詔下各省接濟月餉四十萬兩，江蘇糧台不能時給，疏劾總督怡良、巡撫趙德轍，詔勉其和衷。

translations.literal: When He Chun arrived, pay and arms were both short; an edict ordered all provinces to supply four hundred thousand taels monthly, but the Jiangsu grain bureau could not deliver on time; he memorialized to impeach Governor-General Yiliang and Governor Zhao Dezhe; an edict urged them to work in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chun arrived, pay and supplies were both inadequate. The court ordered the provinces to provide four hundred thousand taels a month, but the Jiangsu grain bureau could not keep up. He impeached Governor-General Yiliang and Governor Zhao Dezhe, and the throne urged all parties to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 溧水、句容為賊精銳所聚，力攻數月，七年夏，先後克之，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Lishui and Jurong were where bandit elites gathered; he attacked fiercely for months; in summer of the seventh year he captured them in succession and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui and Jurong were held by elite rebel forces. He attacked for months, and in the summer of the seventh year captured both in succession. He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 圍攻鎮江，賊數糾悍黨來援，督諸將迭破之。

translations.literal: Besieging Zhenjiang, bandits repeatedly gathered fierce factions to relieve it; he directed the generals in repeated defeats of them.
translations.idiomatic: While besieging Zhenjiang, he faced repeated rebel relief efforts and directed his generals to defeat them one after another.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克鎮江，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he captured Zhenjiang and was granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he captured Zhenjiang and was awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 將軍德興阿督江北諸軍攻瓜洲，同日克復，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: General Dexing'a directed all northern-river armies to attack Guazhou; on the same day it was recovered and military prestige greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: General Dexing'a directed the northern armies against Guazhou, which was recovered the same day. Government morale soared.

sentences.zh: 進攻江寧東北路，奪太平、神策兩門外賊壘。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the northeastern route of Jiangning and seized bandit stockades outside Taiping and Shece gates.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on the northeastern approaches to Jiangning and captured rebel stockades outside Taiping and Shece gates.

sentences.zh: 八年春，賊迭出城，力鬥卻之。

translations.literal: In spring of the eighth year bandits repeatedly came out of the city; he fought fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the rebels sallied repeatedly from the city, but he fought them back each time.

sentences.zh: 合水陸諸​​軍克秣陵關，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Combining land and naval forces he captured Muling Pass and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Combining land and naval forces he captured Muling Pass and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 又破賊三汊河，奪要隘，江寧之圍漸合。

translations.literal: He again defeated bandits at San Cha River, seized strategic passes, and the encirclement of Jiangning gradually closed.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at San Cha River, took the strategic passes, and the encirclement of Jiangning gradually tightened.

sentences.zh: 賊由皖南犯浙境，用以牽掣​​大軍。

translations.literal: Bandits from southern Anhui invaded Zhejiang territory to pin down the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from southern Anhui invaded Zhejiang to tie down the main army.

sentences.zh: 詔和春兼辦浙江軍務，先遣兵二千往援，命親往督師，以病未行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered He Chun also to handle Zhejiang military affairs; he first sent two thousand troops in relief and was ordered to go personally to direct the army, but illness prevented his departure.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was ordered to take charge of military affairs in Zhejiang as well. He first sent two thousand troops to reinforce the province and was ordered to go in person to direct operations, but illness kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 尋浙事緩，罷其行。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zhejiang affairs eased and his journey was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the crisis in Zhejiang eased, and the order for him to go was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 賊复沿江來援，擊走，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Bandits again came along the river in relief; he drove them off and built a long encirclement to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements came again along the river, but he drove them off and built a long encirclement to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊大舉出撲，張國樑破之城下。

translations.literal: In the seventh month bandits came out in force to assault; Zhang Guoliang defeated them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels launched a major assault, but Zhang Guoliang defeated them below the walls.

sentences.zh: 八月，陳玉成糾合捻匪犯江浦、浦口，德興阿兵潰，儀徵、揚州、六合先後陷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chen Yucheng gathered Nian bandits to attack Jiangpu and Pukou; Dexing'a's army collapsed; Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chen Yucheng joined Nian bandits in an attack on Jiangpu and Pukou. Dexing'a's army collapsed, and Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 和春遣馮子材渡江赴援，复失利。

translations.literal: He Chun sent Feng Zicai across the river to relieve them, but again met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun sent Feng Zicai across the river to reinforce them, but the relief force was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 張國樑繼往，力戰，复揚州、儀徵。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang went next, fought fiercely, and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang went next, fought hard, and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，和春授江寧將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month He Chun was appointed General of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month He Chun was appointed General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊乘間出撲，溧水亦陷，急調國樑回援。

translations.literal: Jiangning bandits seized an opening to assault; Lishui also fell; he urgently recalled Guoliang to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Jiangning seized an opening to attack, and Lishui also fell. He urgently recalled Zhang Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 十月，复溧水，而上游賊犯黃池、灣沚，鄧紹良戰沒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he recovered Lishui, but upriver bandits attacked Huangchi and Wanzhi, and Deng Shaoliang was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he recovered Lishui, but rebels from upriver attacked Huangchi and Wanzhi, and Deng Shaoliang was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 九年春，招降捻首薛之元，獻江浦城，复約李世忠破賊，复浦口。

translations.literal: In spring of the ninth year he induced the Nian leader Xue Zhiyuan to surrender and present Jiangpu city; he also arranged with Li Shizhong to defeat bandits and recover Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he induced the Nian leader Xue Zhiyuan to surrender and hand over Jiangpu. He also worked with Li Shizhong to defeat the rebels and recover Pukou.

sentences.zh: 因劾德興阿縱寇狀，詔罷德興阿。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to impeach Dexing'a for allowing bandits to escape; an edict dismissed Dexing'a.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Dexing'a for letting the rebels escape, and the court dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 江北不復置帥，諸軍並歸和春節制。

translations.literal: No commander was again placed over the north of the river; all armies were placed under He Chun's control.
translations.idiomatic: No separate commander was appointed for the north bank, and all forces were placed under He Chun's command.

sentences.zh: 提督鄭魁士亦克灣沚、黃池，進規蕪湖，軍事轉利。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zheng Kuishi also captured Wanzhi and Huangchi and advanced to threaten Wuhu; military affairs turned favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zheng Kuishi also recovered Wanzhi and Huangchi and advanced toward Wuhu. The military situation began to improve.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「揆察現勢，先盡力於金陵一路，絕其根株，則枝葉自萎。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Surveying the present situation, we should first exert all strength on the Jinling route, cut off the roots, and the branches and leaves will wither of themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Given the present situation, we should concentrate all our strength on the Jinling front. Cut off the root, and the branches will wither of themselves.'

sentences.zh: 欲破金陵，必先斷浦口。

translations.literal: To break Jinling, we must first cut off Pukou.'
translations.idiomatic: To take Jinling, we must first cut off Pukou.'

sentences.zh: 請添募精銳萬人，由張國樑統率，一面力攻，一面進扎營壘，斷賊糧路，兼卻外援。

translations.literal: He requested recruitment of ten thousand elite troops under Zhang Guoliang's command, attacking with force on one hand and advancing to encamp on the other, cutting bandit grain routes and also repelling external relief.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recruit ten thousand elite troops under Zhang Guoliang's command to press the attack while establishing camps to cut rebel supply lines and block outside reinforcements.'

sentences.zh: 臣當相度事機，剋期蕆功。

translations.literal: Your servant will gauge the occasion and complete the task within the set term.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall watch for the right moment and complete the task on schedule.'

sentences.zh: 」詔允之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，陳玉成由六合犯揚州，分黨渡江窺秣陵關，欲抄大營後路，東壩、溧水皆告警。

translations.literal: That winter Chen Yucheng from Liuhe attacked Yangzhou; a detachment crossed the river to spy on Muling Pass, intending to strike at the rear of the main camp; Dongba and Lishui were both alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chen Yucheng advanced from Liuhe against Yangzhou. A detachment crossed the river to probe Muling Pass, aiming to strike the main camp from the rear. Dongba and Lishui were both put on alert.

sentences.zh: 尋大舉犯江浦，提督週天培死之，遂陷浦口。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he launched a major attack on Jiangpu; Grand Coordinator Zhou Tianpei died in the fighting, and Pukou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: He soon launched a major attack on Jiangpu. Grand Coordinator Zhou Tianpei was killed in battle, and Pukou fell.

sentences.zh: 張國樑、馮子材援剿獲勝，揚州解嚴，浦口仍為賊踞。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang and Feng Zicai relieved and suppressed them with victory; Yangzhou was relieved from alert, but Pukou remained in bandit hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang and Feng Zicai won a victory in the relief campaign. The alert at Yangzhou was lifted, but Pukou remained in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 十年春，國樑督水陸軍攻九洑洲，大捷，破其老巢。

translations.literal: In spring of the tenth year Guoliang directed land and naval forces to attack Jiufuzhou, won a great victory, and broke their old nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Zhang Guoliang led land and naval forces against Jiufuzhou, won a major victory, and destroyed the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 九洑洲為江寧水陸咽喉，既得，已成合圍之勢，而賊復由皖南犯浙，遽陷杭州，蘇、常震動。

translations.literal: Jiufuzhou was the throat of Jiangning by land and water; once taken, the encirclement was already formed, but bandits again invaded Zhejiang from southern Anhui, swiftly captured Hangzhou, and Suzhou and Changzhou were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiufuzhou was the strategic choke point for Jiangning by land and water. Once it fell, the encirclement was nearly complete. But rebels from southern Anhui invaded Zhejiang, swiftly took Hangzhou, and threw Suzhou and Changzhou into panic.

sentences.zh: 詔和春仍兼辦浙江軍務，先後分兵萬餘，提督張玉良總統赴援，甫至，賊即棄杭州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered He Chun again to handle Zhejiang military affairs; he successively detached more than ten thousand troops; Grand Coordinator Zhang Yuliang was made overall commander to relieve them; as soon as he arrived, the bandits abandoned Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was again ordered to take charge of military affairs in Zhejiang. He sent more than ten thousand troops in stages under Grand Coordinator Zhang Yuliang. As soon as Zhang arrived, the rebels abandoned Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，由廣德分犯建平、東壩、溧陽，遂窺常州，急調張玉良回援，賊已分路迳趨江寧。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month they divided from Guangde to invade Jianping, Dongba, and Liyang, then spied on Changzhou; Zhang Yuliang was urgently recalled, but bandits had already divided routes and marched straight on Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month the rebels advanced from Guangde against Jianping, Dongba, and Liyang, then threatened Changzhou. Zhang Yuliang was urgently recalled, but rebel columns were already marching directly on Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時賊酋陳玉成、李秀成、李侍賢、楊輔清，糾諸路眾十餘萬，力破長圍，城賊應之。

translations.literal: At the time bandit chiefs Chen Yucheng, Li Xiucheng, Li Shixian, and Yang Fuqing gathered more than a hundred thousand from all routes, broke the long encirclement by force, and city bandits responded.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Chen Yucheng, Li Xiucheng, Li Shixian, and Yang Fuqing gathered more than a hundred thousand men from all directions, broke through the encirclement by force, and were joined by the rebels inside the city.

sentences.zh: 大營軍心不固，惟恃張國樑力禦。

translations.literal: The main camp's morale was unsteady; they relied only on Zhang Guoliang's strength to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Morale in the main camp collapsed, and only Zhang Guoliang's fierce resistance held the line.

sentences.zh: 戰數晝夜，諸營同時火起。

translations.literal: They fought for several days and nights; all camps caught fire at once.
translations.idiomatic: The battle raged for days and nights until fires broke out simultaneously in every camp.

sentences.zh: 總兵黃靖、馬登富、吳天爵陣亡，全軍大潰，退守鎮江。

translations.literal: Major Generals Huang Jing, Ma Dengfu, and Wu Tianjue died in battle; the whole army collapsed in rout and withdrew to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Major Generals Huang Jing, Ma Dengfu, and Wu Tianjue were killed in battle. The entire army collapsed and fell back to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 和春坐褫職留軍。

translations.literal: He Chun was stripped of office for the fault but retained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was stripped of rank but allowed to remain with the army.

sentences.zh: 又退丹陽，賊踵至，張國樑死之。

translations.literal: He withdrew again to Danyang; bandits followed close; Zhang Guoliang died there.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back again to Danyang with the rebels in pursuit. Zhang Guoliang was killed there.

sentences.zh: 和春奪圍走常州，督兵迎敵，被重創，退至無錫，卒於軍。

translations.literal: He Chun broke out of the encirclement and fled to Changzhou, directed troops to meet the enemy, was gravely wounded, withdrew to Wuxi, and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun broke out of the encirclement and fled to Changzhou, where he tried to rally troops against the enemy, was gravely wounded, withdrew to Wuxi, and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 總督何桂清棄城走，常州、蘇州相繼陷。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Guiqing abandoned the city and fled; Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Guiqing abandoned his post and fled. Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 江南軍自向榮始任，凡曆七年，至是熸焉，蘇、浙遂糜爛。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan army, from the time Xiang Rong first took charge, had lasted seven years in all; at this point it was extinguished, and Suzhou and Zhejiang were then utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan army, which had begun under Xiang Rong, had lasted seven years. With its collapse, Suzhou and Zhejiang were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔念和春前功，雖兵機屢挫，尚能血戰捐軀，復原官，依例賜卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉，合前世職並為二等男爵，諡忠壯，附祀江寧昭忠祠。

translations.literal: When word arrived, an edict recalled He Chun's earlier merit: although military fortune was repeatedly defeated, he could still fight bloodily and give his life; his original office was restored, condolence grants were given according to regulation, he was granted Commandant of Cavalry together with Commandant of the Cloud Chariots, combined with earlier hereditary offices into a second-class baron, given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, and attached for worship at the Jiangning Zhao Zhong Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the court honored He Chun's earlier achievements: though fortune had repeatedly turned against him, he had fought to the death. His former rank was restored, standard mourning honors were granted, and he was given the combined hereditary rank of second-class baron together with Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of the Cloud Chariots. He received the posthumous name Zhongzhuang and was enshrined at the Jiangning Zhao Zhong Shrine.

sentences.zh: 子霍順武，候選參將，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Huoshunwu was an expectant colonel and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huoshunwu, an expectant colonel, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 張國樑，字殿臣，廣東高要人，初名嘉祥。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang, style name Dianchen, a native of Gaoyao in Guangdong, originally named Jiaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang, courtesy name Dianchen, was a native of Gaoyao in Guangdong. His original name was Jiaxiang.

sentences.zh: 少材武任俠，為裡豪所辱，毀其家，走山澤為盜，不妄殺。

translations.literal: In youth he was talented in martial arts and chivalrous; local bullies humiliated him and destroyed his family; he fled to mountains and marshes to become a bandit and did not kill indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was skilled in arms and lived by a code of honor. Local bullies humiliated him and ruined his family, so he fled to the hills and became an outlaw, but he did not kill indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 流入越南，後歸鎮南關。

translations.literal: He drifted into Vietnam and later returned to Zhennan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He drifted into Vietnam and later returned to Zhennan Pass.

sentences.zh: 按察使勞崇光聞其名，招降，剿匪多得其力。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Lao Chongguang heard his name, induced him to surrender, and in suppressing bandits often gained his help.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Lao Chongguang heard of him, induced him to surrender, and relied on him heavily in suppressing banditry.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，破劇賊顏品瑤，斬於陣，盡殲其黨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he defeated the fierce bandit Yan Pinyao, beheaded him in battle, and annihilated his entire faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he defeated the major bandit Yan Pinyao, killed him in battle, and wiped out his entire band.

sentences.zh: 積功擢守備，繼隸向榮軍。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to garrison commander and afterward served under Xiang Rong's army.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated merit he was promoted to garrison commander and later joined Xiang Rong's army.

sentences.zh: 二年，從解桂林圍，復全州、永興，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in relieving the siege of Guilin, recovered Quanzhou and Yongxing, and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he took part in raising the siege of Guilin, recovered Quanzhou and Yongxing, and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 赴援湖南，迭破賊於醴陵​​、益陽、湘陰。

translations.literal: He went to relieve Hunan and repeatedly defeated bandits at Liling, Yiyang, and Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He went to reinforce Hunan and won repeated victories over the rebels at Liling, Yiyang, and Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 援武昌，戰於洪山，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He relieved Wuchang and fought at Hongshan, serving as assault vanguard in each engagement.
translations.idiomatic: He went to relieve Wuchang and fought at Hongshan, leading the assault in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 三年，至江寧，逼城而軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he reached Jiangning and encamped pressing the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he reached Jiangning and encamped close under the city walls.

sentences.zh: 國樑屯七橋甕，攻鍾山賊壘，先登受傷，溫旨垂問，益感奮，遇艱險，一往直前。

translations.literal: Guoliang encamped at Qiqiao'ao and attacked bandit stockades on Bell Mountain; he was first to scale the walls and was wounded. A gracious edict inquired after him; he was all the more stirred to zeal; encountering hardship and peril, he pressed straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang encamped at Qiqiao'ao and attacked the rebel stockades on Bell Mountain. He was first over the wall and was wounded. The throne sent a gracious inquiry after him, and he fought all the harder, pressing forward through every danger.

sentences.zh: 擢湖南永州營游擊。

translations.literal: He was promoted colonel of the Yongzhou battalion in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to colonel of the Yongzhou battalion in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 雨花台為近城要地，屢力攻，幾克之，賜號霍羅琦巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Yuhuatai was a vital position near the city; he repeatedly attacked with full force and nearly captured it; he was granted the designation Huoluoqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhuatai was a key position near the city walls. He attacked it repeatedly with all his strength and nearly took it. He was granted the title Huoluoqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，复太平。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year he recovered Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he recovered Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太平在江寧上游，賊踞之以通糧運。

translations.literal: Taiping lay upriver from Jiangning; bandits held it to keep grain transport open.
