translations.idiomatic: Taiping lay upriver from Jiangning, and the rebels held it to keep their supply lines open.

sentences.zh: 府城三面阻水，惟東路通陸。

translations.literal: The prefectural city was blocked by water on three sides; only the eastern route connected by land.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural city was bounded by water on three sides, with only the eastern approach open by land.

sentences.zh: 賊聚千艘結四壘，設防甚密。

translations.literal: Bandits gathered a thousand boats and formed four stockades, with very tight defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed a thousand boats and built four stockades with formidable defenses.

sentences.zh: 國樑分三隊進，設伏縱火，自率精銳四百人突賊營，一戰克之，時稱奇捷。

translations.literal: Guoliang advanced in three columns, set ambushes and set fires, personally led four hundred elite troops in a rush on the bandit camp, and captured it in one battle; at the time it was called a marvel of swift victory.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang advanced in three columns, set ambushes and fires, and personally led four hundred elite troops in a charge on the rebel camp. He took it in a single battle, which contemporaries hailed as a marvel of swift victory.

sentences.zh: 擢廣西三江協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted deputy commander of the Sanjiang Brigade in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Sanjiang Brigade in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 又攻雨花台，平賊壘，毀砲台。

translations.literal: He again attacked Yuhuatai, leveled bandit stockades, and destroyed batteries.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yuhuatai again, leveled the rebel stockades, and destroyed the batteries.

sentences.zh: 剿南路竄賊，追入秣陵關，殲戮殆盡。

translations.literal: He suppressed marauding bandits on the southern route, pursued them into Muling Pass, and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued marauding rebels on the southern front into Muling Pass and killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢福建漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted commander of Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 大軍急攻鎮江、瓜洲，江寧賊時出窺伺，江北賊亦乘隙進圖牽制。

translations.literal: The main army pressed the attack on Zhenjiang and Guazhou; Jiangning bandits constantly came out to spy; north-river bandits also seized openings to advance and pin down government forces.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army pressed the attack on Zhenjiang and Guazhou, rebels at Jiangning kept probing for openings, and forces north of the river seized every chance to tie down government troops.

sentences.zh: 國樑隨方截擊，奔命不遑。

translations.literal: Guoliang intercepted them wherever they appeared, racing from crisis to crisis without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang intercepted them wherever they appeared, rushing from one emergency to the next without rest.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊聚倉頭、炭渚、下蜀街，以斷鎮江、江寧之師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year bandits gathered at Cangtou, Tanzhu, and Xiashu Street to cut off the armies at Zhenjiang and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the rebels concentrated at Cangtou, Tanzhu, and Xiashu Street to cut off the armies at Zhenjiang and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 國樑總統諸軍合擊，旬日之間，殺賊萬餘，賊不得逞，乃渡江犯瓜洲，江北諸軍皆潰，又陷江浦、浦口。

translations.literal: Guoliang as overall commander jointly struck them; within ten days he killed more than ten thousand bandits; the bandits could not prevail and then crossed the river to attack Guazhou; all northern armies collapsed, and Jiangpu and Pukou also fell.
translations.idiomatic: As overall commander, Guoliang led a joint assault that killed more than ten thousand rebels in ten days. When the rebels could not hold their ground, they crossed the river against Guazhou. Government forces on the north bank collapsed, and Jiangpu and Pukou fell.

sentences.zh: 國樑馳援，連破賊於毛許墩、葛塘，复江浦、浦口。

translations.literal: Guoliang rushed to relieve them, repeatedly defeated bandits at Maoxudun and Getang, and recovered Jiangpu and Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang hurried to the relief, won successive victories at Maoxudun and Getang, and recovered Jiangpu and Pukou.

sentences.zh: 特詔嘉獎，加提督銜。

translations.literal: A special edict praised and rewarded him, and he was given the rank of Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict commended him and granted him the rank of Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡撫吉爾杭阿戰歿，鎮江告急，溧水被陷，國樑回軍克之，而賊數路趨江寧，夾攻大營。

translations.literal: Before long Governor Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle; Zhenjiang reported urgent peril; Lishui was captured; Guoliang turned his army and recovered it, but bandits came by several routes toward Jiangning and attacked the main camp from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Governor Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle, Zhenjiang sent urgent appeals for help, and Lishui fell. Guoliang turned back and recovered Lishui, but rebel columns converged on Jiangning and attacked the main camp from several directions.

sentences.zh: 向榮不能禦，急調國樑回援，血戰累日，左足被槍傷，偕榮退保丹陽。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong could not hold them off and urgently recalled Guoliang; they fought bloody battles for days; his left foot was wounded by gunfire; together with Rong he withdrew to defend Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong could not hold the line and urgently recalled Guoliang. They fought bloody battles for days until Guoliang was shot in the left foot. Together with Rong he withdrew to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時大江南北諸軍，賊所尤畏者，惟國樑一人。

translations.literal: At the time among all armies north and south of the river, the one the bandits feared most was Guoliang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the armies north and south of the Yangtze, the rebels feared no one more than Zhang Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 賊勢忽南忽北，多方肄我，皆牽制國樑之計，果為所敗。

translations.literal: Bandit power shifted suddenly south and north, harassing government forces on many sides; all were stratagems to pin down Guoliang, and they indeed succeeded in defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shifted their forces suddenly between north and south, harassing government troops on many fronts. It was all designed to tie down Zhang Guoliang, and the strategy worked.

sentences.zh: 榮既病，軍事一倚之。

translations.literal: Once Rong fell ill, military affairs relied entirely on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong fell ill, military affairs depended entirely on Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 將軍福興與國樑不協，詔福興移軍江西，以國樑幫辦江南軍務。

translations.literal: General Fuxing did not cooperate with Guoliang; an edict ordered Fuxing to shift his army to Jiangxi and assigned Guoliang to assist in Jiangnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: General Fuxing could not work with Guoliang. Fuxing was ordered to move his army to Jiangxi, and Guoliang was assigned to assist in military affairs in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 賊屢至，皆挫之。

translations.literal: Bandits came repeatedly and were each time repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked repeatedly, and each time he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 榮卒於軍，命和春代將，未至，國樑激勵將士，解金壇圍，復東壩、高淳，進攻句容。

translations.literal: Rong died in camp; He Chun was ordered to replace him as commander; before He Chun arrived, Guoliang roused the officers and soldiers, lifted the siege of Jintan, recovered Dongba and Gaochun, and advanced to attack Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died in camp, He Chun was ordered to take command. Before He Chun arrived, Guoliang rallied his troops, raised the siege of Jintan, recovered Dongba and Gaochun, and advanced on Jurong.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢湖南提督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Grand Coordinator of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 克句容，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He captured Jurong and was granted a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Jurong and was awarded the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 督諸軍規复鎮江。

translations.literal: He directed the armies in planning recovery of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the armies in the campaign to recover Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 高資為鎮江、江寧要衝，兩路悍賊麕聚力爭，連營二十餘裡，國樑大破之，斬偽安王洪仁等，又連破之於龍潭，援賊盡殲。

translations.literal: Gaozi was the vital junction of Zhenjiang and Jiangning; fierce bandits from both routes gathered and strove for it, encamping in a line of more than twenty li; Guoliang inflicted a great defeat, beheaded the false Prince of An Hong Ren and others, again defeated them repeatedly at Longtan, and annihilated all relief bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozi was the strategic junction between Zhenjiang and Jiangning. Fierce rebel forces from both directions massed there and built camps stretching more than twenty li. Guoliang routed them, killed the rebel Prince of An Hong Ren and others, won further victories at Longtan, and wiped out the relief force.

sentences.zh: 鎮江糧盡援絕，遂克其城，城陷賊已歷五年。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang's grain was exhausted and relief cut off; he then captured the city; it had been in bandit hands for five years.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhenjiang's supplies exhausted and relief cut off, he finally took the city, which had been in rebel hands for five years.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，文宗大悅，詔嘉國樑謀勇超群，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, Emperor Wenzong was greatly pleased; an edict praised Guoliang's surpassing counsel and courage and granted a hereditary rank as Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong was delighted. An edict praised Guoliang's exceptional courage and strategy and granted him the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 於是偕和春進規江寧。

translations.literal: He then advanced with He Chun to plan the recovery of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined He Chun in the campaign against Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 八年，克秣陵關，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he captured Muling Pass and was granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he captured Muling Pass and was awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 复薄江寧城下，自春徂夏，迭戰破賊。

translations.literal: He again pressed close below Jiangning's walls; from spring to summer he fought repeatedly and defeated bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He again pressed close to the walls of Jiangning and, from spring through summer, won a series of victories over the rebels.

sentences.zh: 築長圍，至秋乃成。

translations.literal: He built a long encirclement, which was completed only by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He built a long encirclement that was not complete until autumn.

sentences.zh: 皖賊大舉來援，江浦、浦口、儀徵、揚州、六合先後陷。

translations.literal: Anhui bandits came in force to relieve the city; Jiangpu, Pukou, Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces from Anhui came in strength to relieve the city. Jiangpu, Pukou, Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 國樑渡江援剿，复揚州、儀徵。

translations.literal: Guoliang crossed the river to relieve and suppress them and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang crossed the river to reinforce the northern front and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 調江南提督，晉三等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Grand Coordinator of Jiangnan and advanced to Third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiangnan and promoted to Third-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 然賊仍踵故智，國梁兵至則走，去則復來。

translations.literal: Yet bandits still followed their old trick: when Guoliang's troops arrived they fled, and when he left they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels still used their old tactic: when Guoliang's troops arrived they fled, and when he left they returned.

sentences.zh: 九年，提督週天培戰死江浦，國樑坐褫世職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Grand Coordinator Zhou Tianpei died in battle at Jiangpu; Guoliang was stripped of his hereditary office for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Grand Coordinator Zhou Tianpei was killed at Jiangpu, and Guoliang was stripped of his hereditary rank for the failure.

sentences.zh: 十年，合水陸諸軍克九洑洲，沿江賊爭投款，約期攻上下兩關，招撫五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, combining land and naval forces, he captured Jiufuzhou; bandits along the river competed to surrender; a date was set to attack the upper and lower passes; more than five thousand were induced to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he combined land and naval forces to capture Jiufuzhou. Rebels along the river rushed to surrender, a date was set to attack the upper and lower passes, and more than five thousand were brought over peacefully.

sentences.zh: 軍中方謂堅城旦夕可下，而浙江告警，兵分益單，饋運不繼。

translations.literal: In the army they were just saying the fortified city could fall any day, but Zhejiang sounded the alarm; forces were divided ever thinner, and supply transport could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The army believed the walled city would fall at any moment, but then Zhejiang came under attack. Forces were spread thinner, and supplies could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 和春用翼長王濬策，兵餉三分留一，約待克城後補給，士卒皆怨，國樑力諫不聽。

translations.literal: He Chun adopted Wing Commander Wang Jun's plan to retain only one-third of pay and provisions, promising to make up the rest after the city was taken; the soldiers all resented it; Guoliang remonstrated forcefully but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun adopted Wing Commander Wang Jun's plan to withhold two-thirds of pay and provisions until the city fell. The troops were furious. Guoliang protested strongly, but was not listened to.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，賊猝大至，四路受敵，大營不守，偕和春退丹陽。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month bandits suddenly arrived in force; attacked on four sides, the main camp could not be held; together with He Chun he withdrew to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month the rebels struck suddenly in force. Attacked from four directions, the main camp collapsed, and Guoliang withdrew to Danyang with He Chun.

sentences.zh: 國樑以馮子材在鎮江未敗，進謀扼守。

translations.literal: Guoliang, because Feng Zicai at Zhenjiang had not yet been defeated, advanced to plan a blocking defense.
translations.idiomatic: Because Feng Zicai still held firm at Zhenjiang, Guoliang advanced to plan a blocking defense.

sentences.zh: 尋率師援丹陽，遇賊城外，兵忽潰，策馬渡河，沒於水。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he led troops to relieve Danyang, encountered bandits outside the walls, the army suddenly collapsed, he spurred his horse across the river, and was lost in the water.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led troops to relieve Danyang, encountered rebels outside the walls, and his army suddenly broke. He spurred his horse into the river and was drowned.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗震悼，猶冀其不死，命軍中偵訪，不得。

translations.literal: When word arrived, Emperor Wenzong was deeply shaken; he still hoped Guoliang was alive and ordered the army to search for him, but he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong was deeply grieved. He still hoped Guoliang had survived and ordered a search of the army, but no trace could be found.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，乃下詔優恤，追贈太子太保，祀昭忠祠，諡忠武，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職。

translations.literal: After several months an edict granted generous condolence, posthumously promoted him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Zhao Zhong Shrine, gave the posthumous title Zhongwu, and granted a hereditary office as Commandant of Cavalry together with one Commandant of the Cloud Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the court issued generous mourning honors, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Zhao Zhong Shrine, gave him the posthumous name Zhongwu, and granted the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Commandant of the Cloud Chariots.

sentences.zh: 國樑驍勇無敵，江南恃為長城。

translations.literal: Guoliang was fierce and brave beyond compare; Jiangnan relied on him as its Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang was unrivaled in courage and skill, and Jiangnan relied on him as its bulwark.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，數郡遂淪陷。

translations.literal: At his death several prefectures then fell.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, several prefectures soon fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 士民哀思，私立廟祀。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners mourned him and privately built temples to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry and townspeople mourned him and built private shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 傳述戰績，與古名將同稱，往往附會過實，然益見威烈入人之深。

translations.literal: Accounts of his battles were told on a par with ancient famous generals, often embellished beyond fact, yet this only shows all the more how deeply his martial majesty entered people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Stories of his battles were told alongside those of the great generals of old, often exaggerated beyond what the facts support, yet this only shows how deeply his martial renown had entered the popular imagination.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，江寧克復，偽忠王李秀成就擒，言賊中咸重國樑，禮葬於丹陽尹公橋塔下，乃得遺骸焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, when Jiangning was recovered, the false Prince of Loyalty Li Xiucheng was captured; he said that within the bandits all honored Guoliang and had buried him with ceremony beneath the pagoda at Yingong Bridge in Danyang; only then was his remains obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi, when Jiangning was recovered, the captured rebel Prince of Loyalty Li Xiucheng said that the rebels had all respected Guoliang and buried him with honor beneath the pagoda at Yingong Bridge in Danyang. Only then were his remains recovered.

sentences.zh: 詔加給三等輕車都尉，合前世職並為一等男爵。

translations.literal: An edict added the rank of Third-class Commandant of Light Chariots, combining with earlier hereditary offices into a first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: The court added the rank of Third-class Commandant of Light Chariots, combining it with his earlier honors into the hereditary title of first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 祀江寧忠義祠，復與向榮合建專祠。

translations.literal: He was worshipped in the Jiangning Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a special shrine was again built jointly with Xiang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Jiangning Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and a joint special shrine was built with Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 子廕清，襲男爵。

translations.literal: His son Yinqing inherited the barony.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yinqing inherited the barony.

sentences.zh: 論曰：粵匪初起，向榮與諸帥不和，致無成功，援桂林、長沙，為時所稱，故文宗終用之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the Cantonese bandits first rose, Xiang Rong failed to cooperate with other commanders and therefore achieved no success; his relief of Guilin and Changsha won contemporary praise, and therefore Emperor Wenzong continued to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: When the Cantonese rebellion first broke out, Xiang Rong's failure to cooperate with other commanders cost him success. His relief of Guilin and Changsha won contemporary praise, which is why Emperor Wenzong continued to employ him.

sentences.zh: 其規江南也，近未破鎮江、瓜洲犄角之勢，遠未清長江上游，無以製賊死命，數年支拄，暫保吳疆，固昧遠猷，亦限兵力。

translations.literal: In his planning for Jiangnan, near at hand he had not broken the pincer of Zhenjiang and Guazhou, and far off he had not cleared the upper Yangtze; he had no means to seize the bandits' vital point; for several years he propped up the situation and temporarily preserved the Wu region—this was indeed shortsighted strategy, but also a limit of military strength.
translations.idiomatic: In his planning for Jiangnan, he had not broken the mutually supporting rebel positions at Zhenjiang and Guazhou nearby, nor cleared the upper Yangtze in the distance. He had no way to strike at the rebels' vital center. For years he merely propped up the situation and temporarily preserved the Wu region. This was shortsighted strategy, but also a limit of available force.

sentences.zh: 和春繼克鎮江，又以援浙分兵，垂成之敗，禍更烈焉。

translations.literal: He Chun followed by capturing Zhenjiang, yet again divided forces to relieve Zhejiang; a defeat on the verge of success brought disaster all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun captured Zhenjiang in turn, but then divided his forces to reinforce Zhejiang. A defeat on the verge of victory brought catastrophe all the greater.

sentences.zh: 張國樑一時健者，使盡其用，功不止此。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang was a formidable man of his time; had his talents been fully used, his achievements would not have stopped here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang was the strongest commander of his day. Had his abilities been fully used, his achievements would have been far greater.

sentences.zh: 善夫胡林翼之言曰：「未扼賊吭，江寧原難遽复。

translations.literal: How apt is Hu Linyi's saying: 'Without throttling the bandits' throat, Jiangning was originally hard to recover quickly.'
translations.idiomatic: How apt was Hu Linyi's remark: 'Without throttling the rebels' throat, Jiangning was never going to be recovered quickly.'

sentences.zh: 」觀湘軍之所以成功，與向榮、和春等之所以蹉跌，兵事固無幸焉者矣。

translations.literal: Observing why the Hunan army succeeded and why Xiang Rong, He Chun, and others stumbled, in military affairs there is indeed no room for luck.
translations.idiomatic: Considering why the Hunan army succeeded while Xiang Rong, He Chun, and others failed, it is clear that in war there is no room for luck.
